claim: Lin, Chen, and Yao develop a two-loop unified motion/force/impedance controller for rigid manipulators contacting an initially unknown environment. Recursive least-squares estimation identifies a decoupled Kelvin-Voigt contact model; an outer model-predictive quadratic program replans motion and force references subject to estimated contact, velocity, acceleration, and force constraints; and an inner robust model-reaching law drives a generalized target model whose matrices trade motion against force tracking. The authors prove bounded parameter-estimation error and target-model reaching under known bounds on plant uncertainty and disturbance. Franka Panda experiments report smoother unknown-contact transitions and a better free-space/compliance compromise than the tested impedance and admittance baselines, plus simultaneous two-axis motion and force tracking. The guarantee does not remove the need for uncertainty bounds, sufficient contact excitation, a stable single decoupled contact, exact force sensing, or feasible real-time optimization, and the paper explicitly notes that time-varying inertia or stiffness can destroy passivity.
epistemic_status: qualified primary analytical and hardware evidence: bounded estimation and target-model reaching are proved for the stated rigid-manipulator, bounded-uncertainty, decoupled Kelvin-Voigt setting; performance superiority is author-reported from a small number of Franka experiments without uncertainty intervals or statistical testing
problem_and_setting: Automated assembly and similar tasks require fast, accurate free-space motion followed by compliant, force-regulated contact despite unknown contact position and stiffness. The paper seeks a single control framework that can move smoothly among motion, force, impedance, and hybrid objectives without assuming the environment model is known before contact.
method_or_mechanism: A generalized target model links replanned motion error and force error through time-varying desired inertia, damping, stiffness, and force weighting. In the outer loop, recursive least squares estimates each decoupled environment direction's stiffness and damping after the first-contact equilibrium position is recorded. A receding-horizon quadratic program selects motion and force references close to the user's desired references while enforcing estimated Kelvin-Voigt dynamics and kinematic/force bounds. In the inner loop, a dynamic compensator and sliding function define robust model-reaching control; a discontinuous term sized from known model-error and disturbance bounds forces the sliding variables toward zero, thereby recovering the target model.
content_summary: The paper formulates rigid-manipulator Cartesian dynamics with bounded model, friction, and disturbance errors and a stable, single-contact Kelvin-Voigt environment. Theorem 1 shows uniform boundedness of the recursive least-squares parameter error under the selected covariance law. Theorem 2 shows convergence of the robust model-reaching sliding variable and realization of the target model when the robust gain exceeds the stated uncertainty bound. Experiments use a seven-DOF Franka Emika Panda with an ATI Nano25 sensor at 1 kHz; estimation also runs at 1 kHz and trajectory adaptation at 200 Hz. Four controllers are compared during contact with a deformable plastic surface and a stiffer surface. The proposed controller with trajectory adaptation shows lower impact/second-contact behavior than its no-adaptation version and the tested admittance controller while tracking free motion better than the tested impedance controller. A separate inclined-surface experiment steps desired forces to 5 and 10 N in Z and 2.5 and 5 N in Y and reports concurrent tracking, with measured force noise around plus or minus 0.2 N.
synthesis_role: Provides a systems-level example of unifying mode transitions through online environment estimation, constrained trajectory replanning, and a robust target-model inner loop. It supports feasibility on hardware but is not evidence of passivity-preserving variable impedance or broad robustness across contact regimes.
development_link: The work extends generalized model-reaching control by adding estimated-environment trajectory adaptation, and extends prior unified impedance/admittance switching approaches to include force tracking and unknown-contact experiments. It also exposes a boundary shared with many variable-impedance schemes: changing target inertia or stiffness can inject energy unless additional passivity handling is used.

evidence.finding: The controller is developed for a rigid manipulator with bounded model/friction/disturbance errors and a fully decoupled stable single-contact Kelvin-Voigt environment with unknown equilibrium position, stiffness, and damping.
The recursive least-squares covariance law yields uniformly bounded environment-parameter error; accurate damping estimation still requires sufficient excitation during sustained contact.
A real-time quadratic program replans force and motion references to satisfy estimated contact dynamics and velocity, acceleration, and force bounds while remaining close to desired references.
The authors show that increasing desired inertia or stiffness can add energy and destroy passivity during target-model variation.
With known uncertainty bounds and a sufficiently large discontinuous robust term, the sliding variable converges and the manipulator reaches the selected generalized target model.
Validation uses a torque-controlled seven-DOF Franka Panda, ATI Nano25 force/torque sensor, 1 ms controller/estimator periods, and a 5 ms trajectory-replanning period.

Across a deformable and a stiffer contact surface, trajectory adaptation reduces the initial mismatch and contact force relative to the same model-reaching controller without adaptation; the tested impedance and admittance baselines show the expected free-motion/compliance trade-off.

On an inclined surface, the controller replans references, estimates stiffness/damping, and tracks stepped force commands simultaneously in two directions, with reported force noise of plus or minus 0.2 N.

boundary_conditions: The environment is modeled as stable, single-contact, linear Kelvin-Voigt dynamics that are fully decoupled across Cartesian dimensions.
Environment equilibrium position is initialized at first contact, and reliable damping estimation requires persistent or adequate excitation that may not occur during contact establishment.
The robust model-reaching gain requires known upper bounds on inertia, Coriolis, gravity, friction, modeling error, and external disturbance discrepancies.
The discontinuous s divided by norm(s) term is analyzed ideally; chattering, smoothing, sensor quantization, and actuator bandwidth are not incorporated in the theorem.
The trajectory-adaptation QP must remain feasible and solve within 5 ms; infeasibility, solver failures, and computational worst cases are not evaluated.
Changing target inertia or stiffness is not passivity-preserving in general, and no energy tank or passivity filter is added.
Experiments cover two contact surfaces and one inclined tracking task on one platform, with no repetition count, variance, confidence interval, or statistical test.
The target-model thresholds and matrices are hand selected; automatic selection and contact-rich assembly are left as future work.
assumptions: Rigid-manipulator dynamics and Cartesian mapping satisfy the stated boundedness and positive-definiteness properties.
External force/moment is measured accurately and aligned with the modeled Cartesian contact dimensions.
The environment remains within the decoupled Kelvin-Voigt family during each estimation and replanning interval.
The uncertainty bounds used to choose the robust gain dominate actual modeling errors and disturbances.
Reference and target-model variation are sufficiently smooth for the dynamic compensator and controller derivation.
The QP constraints and desired references admit a feasible replanned trajectory at every update.

reported: Impedance control in the comparison is compliant but has poorer free-space motion tracking.
Admittance control improves free-space tracking but produces larger contact force and more serious second contact on the stiff surface.
The proposed controller without trajectory adaptation experiences larger contact force because position and velocity mismatches remain at contact.
Environment damping cannot be estimated accurately during first contact without sufficient excitation.
Variation of target inertia or stiffness may destroy passivity.
inferred: Underestimated uncertainty bounds can invalidate the reaching proof, whereas large conservative bounds can increase switching effort and chattering.
Coupled, nonlinear, hysteretic, or intermittently separating contacts can bias the estimator and make the QP constraints physically wrong.
Real-time QP infeasibility or delay could reintroduce the transition mismatch that the outer loop is intended to remove.
The limited unreplicated hardware set cannot establish reliability across payloads, contact angles, sensor noise levels, or industrial cycle counts.
